requirements.title: A, AT, and G character editing item rules
requirements.definition: A editing is used with a character effective item; AT is used with a character effective item in output only and shall not be used for input; G may edit character data; character kind is implied by the effective item.

pending.AT-input-invalid: Negative source shape: READ('xy','(AT)') c; repair to A editing. The sole changed property is using AT for input; no diagnostic phase or message is asserted.
pending.kind-implied-by-item: Source-control only for nondefault character kinds: the corresponding item kind selects the transfer kind, but kind availability and representation are processor dependent.

S13.7.4-001 character-editing runtime fixtures: two complete internal-file positive-control programs discharge selected A and G character facets. WRITE(field,'(A2)') 'xy' expects exactly 'xy', proving A editing with a default-character effective item, and WRITE(field,'(G0)') 'xy' expects exactly 'xy' by the 13.7.5.4 G0-as-A dependency. Descriptor substitutions A2->A1 and G0->A1 are load-bearing. AT facets remain pending in this packet because the f2023 reference rejects the AT descriptor, so there is no reference-validated fixture to ship.

requirements.definition: On A input, if w is at least the item length, the rightmost item-length characters are taken; if w is shorter, the field characters become left justified with trailing blanks in the internal value.

requirements.title: AT output trims trailing blanks and all-blank values produce no output
requirements.definition: AT field width is the length after trailing blanks are removed; output is that trimmed value, and all-blank values produce no output by the descriptor.

pending.AT-all-blank-produces-no-output: WRITE(buf,'(AT,"Z")') '   '; expect exactly 'Z' because AT transmits no characters and the following string descriptor writes at the current position.

requirements.title: Character output containing NEW_LINE characters may split stream records as slash editing
requirements.definition: For stream access, non-newline characters are written successively and each NEW_LINE character causes slash-like record termination and creation of a new current record.
